text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: control-plane error rate > 2% for 5m (5xx + gateway timeouts). Sources showing spikes from auth, org-lookup, and billing proxies. Paging SRE oncall. Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CP/ctrlplane-errors, runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/ops/ctrlplane-5xx-runbook

timothy (oncall): Acked. Seeing ~3.8% 5xx cluster-wide, spikes concentrated on /v1/org/lookup and /v1/auth/validate. Full-request lat p95 up from 60ms -> 420ms. Rolling traces show upstream billing timeouts and auth token service 503s.

maria (sre): On it. Can someone confirm recent controlplane config rollout? also pinging eng team that owns org-lookup.

jamie (eng): we pushed a config-service rollout 20m ago that tightened upstream timeout behavior for a subset of calls (commit ab12cd3). It increased aggressive retry/backoff behavior in the proxy. I can revert.

ben (prodops): We observed org-lookup returning 503s and a sudden surge in concurrency. Autoscaling fired but upstream rate-limiter appears to be rejecting. Suggest toggling proxy circuit-breaker to open sooner to protect dependent services.

timothy (oncall): Triage/mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily rollback config-service change to restore previous timeout/retry behavior. 2) Add short-term routing fallback for read-only org lookups to cached responses (prefix cache). 3) Lower org-lookup concurrency limit at the gateway / enable 429->deprioritize policy. 4) Notify CS for customer-facing comms. Who can run the rollback?

jamie (eng): Doing rollback now. Command: 
```bash
kubectl -n controlplane set image deploy/config-service config-service=redwood/config-service:ab12cd2 # rollback to previous stable
```
Rolling pod restarts starting. Watching logs.

jamie (eng): logs: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z config-service rollout started (rev ab12cd2)
2026-03-15T14:03:08Z healthcheck ok on new pods
2026-03-15T14:04:30Z config-service: proxy-timeouts restored to 50ms
```

maria (sre): Starting on quick KG (cached) fallback for org lookup reads. Will flip a routing flag at the gateway to prefer cache for /v1/org/lookup?readOnly=true. Patch coming in 2m.

ben (prodops): Pushed temporary gateway change to reduce forwarded concurrency: 
```json
{"org_lookup_max_inflight": 200, "deprioritize_on_429": true}
```
Applied and monitoring.

incidents-bot: Pager: paged oncall timothy -> acknowledged. Escalation policy: if 5xx > 2% for 10m, page infra-lead.

carla (customer-success): we've got 4 customer tickets about API failures and one Slack thread. Need ETA and brief we can paste. Any guidance?

maria (sre): Quick impact summary for CS: ~3-4% of control-plane requests failed intermittently in last 15m. Affected endpoints: /v1/auth/validate, /v1/org/lookup (read path), and billing metadata fetches. Root cause suspected: recent config rollout increased retry/backoff leading to upstream pressure and timeouts; rolling back now. ETA: monitoring for stabilization in next 5-10m.

timothy (oncall): Handing off active watch to sre-standby-bot. If error rate doesn't drop below 1% in 10m escalate to infra-lead and page channel #exec-ops. Otherwise we keep monitoring and start collecting traces for postmortem. :thumbsup:

sre-standby-bot: Took watch from timothy. Alert policy adjusted to mute noisy alerts for config-service during rollback. Monitoring graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CP/ctrlplane-errors?org_lookup=1

jamie (eng): Rollback finished. New pods stable. Observed immediate drop in auth 5xx but org-lookup still has elevated 502s from upstream for a bit (health of upstream).

maria (sre): Cache fallback flip completed. Preliminary numbers: total 5xx now 0.9% and falling, org-lookup errors down to 1.2% from 4.5%. Continuing sampling traces.

timothy (oncall): Nice work team. Please add any relevant logs/traces to the incident doc (incident id: INC-20260315-17). CS, paste this to customers: "We experienced elevated control-plane errors due to a recent config rollout that increased upstream pressure. We rolled back the change and enabled short-term cache fallbacks; service is stabilizing now. Engineers are monitoring and doing a full investigation."

carla (customer-success): Thank you — will share. Let me know if we need to open an incident comms Slack post.

jamie (eng): I'll follow up with a PR that adds safer rollout defaults and a feature flag for proxy retry/backoff.

maria (sre): Action items for postmortem: timeline, root cause (config retry/backoff + upstream rate-limiter), mitigations applied (rollback, cache fallback, gateway deprioritize), customer impact (approx % requests and known tickets), and follow-up fixes. I'll create the incident doc and assign owners.

incidents-bot: Monitoring: incident still open. 5xx trend dropping. Next update in 10m or on handoff.

sre-standby-bot: Watching; if any regression I'll page back to timothy. Closing note (preliminary): system showing healthy after rollback and fallback.

timothy (oncall): Closing handoff to standby. Thanks all. If anything else crops up tag me.
